heading: INT. BLACKSMITH'S SHOP - TOWN OF DRY CREEK - DAY

units.text: INT. BLACKSMITH'S SHOP - TOWN OF DRY CREEK - DAY
A low-beamed smithy.
A forge glows orange in the back; hammers and tongs hang from the wall like surgical tools.
Heat shimmers off the anvil.
Through the open double door, a dusty street baking in the sun, a horse tied to a rail, a church steeple, and a single wooden gallows frame at the far end of town, no rope yet.
MARSHAL WEBB (50s, long duster, tarnished star, a face the color of saddle leather) sits on a barrel, loading shells into a shotgun one at a time.
The metallic click is steady and unhurried.
LAURENT (40s, the smith, leather apron, forearms scarred by a thousand burns) works the bellows, eyes on the coals.
He hasn't spoken since the Marshal walked in.
DOC AMBROSE (60s, black frock coat, round spectacles, a physician's bag) leans in the doorway, polishing his glasses on a handkerchief.
SISSY (teen, calico dress, a bundle of laundry on her hip) stands behind the anvil, glancing between the men.
How long till the horses are shod?
units.name: WEBB

units.text: Three hours.
units.name: LAURENT

units.text: I need them in two.
units.name: WEBB

units.text: Then you need another smith.
units.name: LAURENT

units.text: Webb clicks another shell home.
Laurent pulls the bellows.
Sparks dance.
The heat builds.
Gentlemen. It's a hot day.
units.name: DOC AMBROSE

units.text: Doc, stay out of it.
units.name: WEBB

units.text: I only observe that tempers rise with the temperature.
units.name: DOC AMBROSE

units.text: Then close the door and let him cook.
units.name: LAURENT

units.text: Sissy shifts her bundle and takes a half-step toward the door.
Girl. Stay put.
units.name: WEBB

units.text: My mother expects me.
units.name: SISSY

units.text: Your mother can wait.
units.name: WEBB

units.text: Sissy stops.
The bellows sigh.
Webb finishes loading, snaps the shotgun shut, and rests it across his knees.
Laurent. The Tarrant boys will be in town by sundown.
units.name: WEBB

units.text: I heard.
units.name: LAURENT

units.text: You were their father's friend.
units.name: WEBB

units.text: I shod their father's mule. That's not friendship.
units.name: LAURENT

units.text: It is, in these parts.
units.name: DOC AMBROSE

units.text: They want the man we've got in the jail.
units.name: WEBB

units.text: Then give him to them.
units.name: LAURENT

units.text: He's a murderer.
units.name: WEBB

units.text: So are they.
units.name: LAURENT

units.text: Webb stands.
Slowly.
He walks to the forge, holding the shotgun at his hip, and looks down at the coals.
The orange light carves his face into hard planes.
I'm not giving anyone to anyone, Laurent. I'm asking you to put a shoe on a horse so I can ride out and meet them in daylight.
units.name: WEBB

units.text: And if you don't come back?
units.name: LAURENT

units.text: Then the shoe wasn't any good.
units.name: WEBB

units.text: Laurent lifts a glowing horseshoe from the coals with tongs.
Webb doesn't flinch.
The metal hisses as Laurent drops it on the anvil and raises his hammer.
If I might suggest, Marshal, the gallows could use a rope.
units.name: DOC AMBROSE

units.text: I know what the gallows needs.
units.name: WEBB

units.text: The hammer falls.
Once.
Twice.
Sissy flinches at the clang.
Outside, a dog barks and a distant bell tolls the hour.
Webb sets the shotgun down on the anvil.
Laurent. After this one, shoe them all.
units.name: WEBB

units.text: I will.
units.name: LAURENT

units.text: The hammer swings again, steady as a heartbeat, and the heat in the smithy builds and builds.
